The UI renders Pakistani rupees with `₨`; the API, database, and LLM keep ISO `PKR` for precision.\\n- 21 automated tests covering leaks, precision, API flow, and guardrails.\\n\\n## Architecture\\n\\n```text\\nBrowser (vanilla JS)\\n        |\\n        v\\nFastAPI /api/v1\\n        |\\n        +-- extract PDF/DOCX/CSV/TXT in memory\\n        +-- local deterministic scrubber\\n        +-- residual-PII guard\\n        +-- transaction parser + deterministic facts\\n        |\\n        v\\nPostgreSQL (scrubbed text, files, redactions, transactions, analyses, chats)\\n        |\\n        v\\nGroq openai/gpt-oss-120b\\n   analysis: compact facts + scrubbed excerpt + transaction digest\\n   chat:     facts + retrieved scrubbed rows + validated analysis\\n```\\n\\n## Quick start\\n\\n### 1. Prerequisites\\n\\n- Python 3.12+\\n- Docker (for PostgreSQL 16)\\n- A Groq API key from [console.groq.com](https://console.groq.com)\\n\\n### 2. Install\\n\\n```bash\\ngit clone https://github.com/MRoshaan/pj-bank-api.git\\ncd pj-bank-api\\npython3 -m venv .venv\\n.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt\\ncp .env.example .env\\n```\\n\\nEdit `.env` and set `GROQ_API_KEY`. The key is never committed.\\n\\n### 3. Start PostgreSQL\\n\\nThe host used for development does not have the Docker Compose plugin, so the tested command is `docker run`:\\n\\n```bash\\ndocker run --name pj-bank-db \\\\\\n  -e POSTGRES_USER=pjbank \\\\\\n  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pjbank_dev_password \\\\\\n  -e POSTGRES_DB=pjbank \\\\\\n  -p 5432:5432 \\\\\\n  -v pjbank_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data \\\\\\n  -d postgres:16\\n```\\n\\nA `docker-compose.yml` is included for environments that have Compose.\\n\\nCreate the test database and tables:\\n\\n```bash\\ndocker exec pj-bank-db psql -U pjbank -d postgres -c \\\"CREATE DATABASE pjbank_test;\\\" || true\\n.venv/bin/python scripts/init_db.py\\n```\\n\\n### 4. Omit it to generate files only.\\n\\n## API\\n\\n| Method | Path | Purpose |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `POST` | `/api/v1/batches` | Multipart upload; scrub, parse, store |\\n| `GET` | `/api/v1/batches` | Recent batches |\\n| `GET` | `/api/v1/batches/{id}` | Batch detail |\\n| `GET` | `/api/v1/batches/{id}/scrubbed` | Combined scrubbed text download |\\n| `GET` | `/api/v1/batches/{id}/transactions` | Filter by category/merchant |\\n| `POST` | `/api/v1/batches/{id}/analyze` | Generate Groq analysis |\\n| `GET` | `/api/v1/batches/{id}/analysis` | Latest analysis |\\n| `POST` | `/api/v1/batches/{id}/chat` | Grounded chat |\\n| `GET` | `/api/v1/batches/{id}/chat/sessions/{sid}` | Chat history |\\n| `GET` | `/api/v1/health` | DB + Groq configuration |\\n\\nExample:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl -X POST http://<IP_ADDRESS>:8000/api/v1/batches \\\\\\n  -F \\\"name=April statements\\\" \\\\\\n  -F \\\"files=<PAYMENT_HANDLE>/wallet_transactions.csv\\\"\\n```\\n\\n## Database schema\\n\\n| Table | Purpose |\\n|---|---|\\n| `batches` | One upload run; combined scrubbed text, counts, facts, warnings |\\n| `statement_files` | Per-file scrubbed text, hash, format, counts, warnings |\\n| `redactions` | Entity type + placeholder + count (never original values) |\\n| `transactions` | Date, time, description, merchant, category, signed amount, currency, balance, source line |\\n| `analyses` | Model, prompt version, JSON result, markdown, grounding report, usage |\\n| `chat_sessions` | Conversation per batch |\\n| `chat_messages` | User/assistant turns, citations, grounding metadata |\\n\\nAll tables use UUID primary keys and cascade deletes. `statement_files.batch_id`, `transactions.batch_id`, `analyses.batch_id`, and chat tables are indexed. Amounts use `NUMERIC(18,2)`, not floats.\\n\\n`schema.sql` contains the PostgreSQL DDL.\\n\\n### Why this schema\\n\\n- Normalizing files and transactions makes per-file output, filtering, and deterministic aggregation possible.\\n- `transactions` is the source of truth for chat and analysis; the LLM never computes totals.\\n- `analyses` is versioned by model/prompt so a later run does not overwrite an earlier result.\\n- `chat_messages` stores citations and grounding metadata for auditability.\\n- No raw statement column exists. ## Assistant

I found gaps in the privacy safeguards: analysis responses can be stored without output scrubbing, and outbound checks omit parts of the assembled chat prompt. I also found duplicate filenames can mix up transaction sources, and ZIP expansion can exceed the upload limits. I’m fixing these and adding regression tests.

def zip_bytes(entries):
    import io
    import zipfile

    stream = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(stream, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as archive:
        for name, content in entries:
            archive.writestr(name, content)
    return stream.getvalue()

    filename: str,

    if not zipfile.is_zipfile(io.BytesIO(content)):
        raise ExtractionError("Not a valid ZIP archive.")
    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(content)) as archive:
            selected = []
            total = 0
            # Check all declared sizes/counts before allocating decompressed data.
            for info in archive.infolist():
                if info.is_dir():
                    continue
                name = info.filename.replace("\\\\\\\\", "/")
                if name.startswith("/") or ".." in name.split("/"):
                    raise ExtractionError("Unsafe path in ZIP archive.")
                base = Path(name).name
                if not base or base.startswith(".") or "__MACOSX" in name.split("/"):
                    continue
                if len(selected) >= max_files:
                    raise ExtractionLimitError("ZIP expansion exceeds the batch file count limit.")
                if info.file_size > max_file_bytes:
                    raise ExtractionLimitError("ZIP member exceeds the per-file size limit.")
                total += info.file_size
                if total > max_total_bytes:
                    raise ExtractionLimitError("ZIP expansion exceeds the total batch size limit.")
                selected.append((base, info))
            return [(base, archive.read(info)) for base, info in selected]
    except (zipfile.BadZipFile, RuntimeError, NotImplementedError, OSError) as exc:
        raise ExtractionError("Could not read ZIP archive.") from exc

new_prepare = '''def _safe_filename(name: str) -> str:
    base = Path(name.replace("\\\\\\\\", "/")).name
    base = re.sub(r"[\\\\x00-\\\\x1f\\\\x7f]", "_", base)
    suffix = Path(base).suffix
    stem = base[:-len(suffix)] if suffix else base
    safe = scrub_text(stem)
    if safe.residual:
        raise PipelineError("Filename contains an identifier after scrubbing.")
    # Keep the extension for format detection and use portable placeholder names.
    stem = safe.text.translate(str.maketrans({"<": "_", ">": "_", "/": "_", "\\\\\\\\": "_"}))
    return (stem[:200] or "unnamed") + suffix[:16]


def _prepare_sources(uploads: Iterable[tuple[str, bytes]]) -> list[tuple[str, bytes]]:
    prepared: list[tuple[str, bytes]] = []
    used: set[str] = set()
    total = 0
    max_file = settings.max_file_mb * 1024 * 1024
    max_total = settings.max_total_mb * 1024 * 1024

    def add(name: str, data: bytes) -> None:
        nonlocal total
        if len(prepared) >= settings.max_files:
            raise UploadLimitError("Upload exceeds the batch file count limit.")
        if len(data) > max_file:
            raise UploadLimitError("A file exceeds the per-file size limit.")
        total += len(data)
        if total > max_total:
            raise UploadLimitError("Upload exceeds the total batch size limit.")
        safe_name = _safe_filename(name)
        path = Path(safe_name)
        counter = 2
        candidate = safe_name
        while candidate.casefold() in used:
            candidate = f"{path.stem}-{counter}{path.suffix}"
            counter += 1
        used.add(candidate.casefold())
        prepared.append((candidate, data))

    for name, content in uploads:
        if len(content) > max_file:
            raise UploadLimitError("A file exceeds the per-file size limit.")
        safe_name = _safe_filename(name)
        if safe_name.lower().endswith(".zip"):
            try:
                members = expand_zip(
                    safe_name,
                    content,
                    max_files=settings.max_files - len(prepared),
                    max_file_bytes=max_file,
                    max_total_bytes=max_total - total,
                )
                for member, data in members:
                    add(member, data)
            except ExtractionLimitError as exc:
                raise UploadLimitError(str(exc)) from exc
            except ExtractionError as exc:
                raise PipelineError(str(exc)) from exc
        else:
            add(safe_name, content)
    return prepared
'''

API\\n\\n## Research and alternatives\\n\\nI <NATIONAL_ID> Microsoft Presidio, scrubadub, spaCy NER, and LLM-based redaction. All were rejected as the primary engine: Presidio/scrubadub/LLM redaction over-scrub person names, which the brief requires preserving, and NER adds a heavy model plus nondeterminism. I chose a local, deterministic span-based engine using labeled context, IBAN mod-97, Luhn, `phonenumbers`, and date/amount exclusions. Python-docx, pdfplumber (MIT; PyMuPDF is AGPL), and charset-normalizer cover the formats. The scrubber preserves masked card last-4 but removes masked bank/wallet identifiers, keeps merchant URLs, and fails closed on residual PII.\\n\\n## API and database\\n\\nThe API is resource-oriented: `POST /api/v1/batches` performs upload → in-memory extraction → scrub → parse → persist atomically. Keeping scrubbing inside the create action means raw text is never written to a staging table. Subresources expose scrubbed text, transactions, analysis, and chat sessions. Folder processing is a CLI, not an HTTP path parameter, to avoid exposing server filesystem paths.\\n\\nPostgreSQL normalizes `batches`, `statement_files`, `redactions`, `transactions`, `analyses`, `chat_sessions`, and `chat_messages`. The `transactions` table is the deterministic source of truth for chat/analysis; `analyses` is versioned by model/prompt; `redactions` stores counts and placeholders only, never originals. No raw statement column exists. UUIDs, `NUMERIC(18,2)`, JSONB for flexible facts/reports, and cascade deletes keep the schema auditable and safe.\\n\\n## LLM model\\n\\nI <NATIONAL_ID> `openai/gpt-oss-120b` on Groq's free tier: 131K context, 30 RPM/1K RPD/8K TPM/200K TPD, strong reasoning, JSON mode, ~500 tokens/sec. `gpt-oss-20b` is faster but weaker; Qwen 3.8 27B is preview and higher-cost; Llama 3.3 70B left the free/developer tier in August 2026. The 8K TPM limit is why analysis sends a compact facts pack, a 3K-character scrubbed excerpt, and a complete transaction digest, not the full combined corpus. Chat uses facts plus retrieved rows, not the whole statement.\\n\\n## System prompt\\n\\nThe analysis system prompt defines the role, treats statement text as untrusted data, makes FACTS the only source of truth for numbers, forbids invented transactions/amounts, requires per-currency reporting, requires transaction refs, and specifies a strict JSON schema. Chat uses the same rules plus “refuse when the context is insufficient” and a JSON answer/citations/figures schema. Output is parsed with Pydantic; invalid JSON gets one repair attempt.\\n\\n## Hallucination and accuracy\\n\\nPython computes all totals, category sums, merchant rankings, balances, fees, cash, and transfers. The LLM writes narrative only. After generation, a deterministic citation-grounding pass replaces model-chosen refs with rows that match the claim’s category/merchant/currency, and every currency/decimal/percentage claim is checked against the allowed fact values. Invalid citations are filtered; unsupported numbers trigger one repair retry, then a deterministic facts-based fallback. All were rejected as the primary engine: Presidio/scrubadub/LLM redaction over-scrub person names, which the brief requires preserving, and NER adds a heavy model plus nondeterminism. I chose a local, deterministic span-based engine using labeled context, IBAN mod-97, Luhn, `phonenumbers`, and date/amount exclusions. Python-docx, pdfplumber (MIT; PyMuPDF is AGPL), and charset-normalizer cover the formats. The scrubber preserves masked card last-4 but removes masked bank/wallet identifiers, keeps merchant URLs, and fails closed on residual PII.\\n\\n## API and database\\n\\nThe API is resource-oriented: `POST /api/v1/batches` performs upload → in-memory extraction → scrub → parse → persist atomically. Keeping scrubbing inside the create action means raw text is never written to a staging table. Subresources expose scrubbed text, transactions, analysis, and chat sessions. Folder processing is a CLI, not an HTTP path parameter, to avoid exposing server filesystem paths.\\n\\nPostgreSQL normalizes `batches`, `statement_files`, `redactions`, `transactions`, `analyses`, `chat_sessions`, and `chat_messages`. The `transactions` table is the deterministic source of truth for chat/analysis; `analyses` is versioned by model/prompt; `redactions` stores counts and placeholders only, never originals. No raw statement column exists. UUIDs, `NUMERIC(18,2)`, JSONB for flexible facts/reports, and cascade deletes keep the schema auditable and safe.\\n\\n## LLM model\\n\\nI <NATIONAL_ID> `openai/gpt-oss-120b` on Groq's free tier: 131K context, 30 RPM/1K RPD/8K TPM/200K TPD, strong reasoning, JSON mode, ~500 tokens/sec. `gpt-oss-20b` is faster but weaker; Qwen 3.8 27B is preview and higher-cost; Llama 3.3 70B left the free/developer tier in August 2026. The 8K TPM limit is why analysis sends a compact facts pack, a 3K-character scrubbed excerpt, and a complete transaction digest, not the full combined corpus. Chat uses facts plus retrieved rows, not the whole statement.\\n\\n## System prompt\\n\\nThe analysis system prompt defines the role, treats statement text as untrusted data, makes FACTS the only source of truth for numbers, forbids invented transactions/amounts, requires per-currency reporting, requires transaction refs, and specifies a strict JSON schema. Chat uses the same rules plus “refuse when the context is insufficient” and a JSON answer/citations/figures schema. Output is parsed with Pydantic; invalid JSON gets one repair attempt.\\n\\n## Hallucination and accuracy\\n\\nPython computes all totals, category sums, merchant rankings, balances, fees, cash, and transfers. The LLM writes narrative only. After generation, a deterministic citation-grounding pass replaces model-chosen refs with rows that match the claim’s category/merchant/currency, and every currency/decimal/percentage claim is checked against the allowed fact values. Invalid citations are filtered; unsupported numbers trigger one repair retry, then a deterministic facts-based fallback. Chat has deterministic fallbacks for food/category spend, top merchant, total spend, fees, cash, transfers, and income. Common capture errors are also handled: the PDF’s split IBAN, masked card vs. bank account, `Netflix.com` vs. email, dates/timestamps vs. long refs, and Indian/German amount formats.\\n\\n## Guardrails and testing\\n\\nEvery Groq payload is re-scanned by the residual-PII detector immediately before the call; chat input is scrubbed before storage/sending; LLM output is scrubbed and scanned before display. Statement data is delimited and never followed as instructions. Additional guards: upload size/type limits, zip-slip protection, JSON schema validation, token/history bounds, 429/5xx retry with model fallback, no raw-text logging. `pytest` covers known-PII absence, merchant/amount/date preservation, idempotence, all four formats, transaction parsing, API flow, prompt injection, residual-PII blocking, numeric/citation validation, and deterministic fallbacks: **21 tests pass**.\\n\\n## Limitations and next steps\\n\\nNo OCR for scanned PDFs; addresses depend on labels; rare ID formats/layouts need new rules; no FX conversion; parser coverage is not universal. With more time I would add OCR, a labeled-address model, per-country rule packs, Alembic migrations, background analysis jobs, and a larger adversarial evaluation set. These limits help ensure service stability, fair access, and protection against misuse so that we can serve reliable and fast inference for all.\\n\\n## Understanding Rate Limits\\n\\nRate limits are measured in:\\n\\n  * RPM: Requests per minute\\n  * RPD: Requests per day\\n  * TPM: Tokens per minute\\n  * TPD: Tokens per day\\n  * ASH: Audio seconds per hour\\n  * ASD: Audio seconds per day\\n  * ITPM: Input tokens per minute\\n  * OTPM: Output tokens per minute\\n\\nCached tokens do not count towards your rate limits.\\n\\nRate limits apply at the organization level, not individual users. You can hit any limit type depending on which threshold you reach first.\\n\\nExample: Let's say your RPM = 50 and your TPM = 200K. If you were to send 50 requests with only 100 tokens within a minute, you would reach your limit even though you did not send 200K tokens within those 50 requests.\\n\\n### Input and Output Token Rate Limits (ITPM / OTPM)\\n\\nIn addition to the combined TPM limit, some organizations are also subject to separate per-minute limits on input tokens (ITPM) and output tokens (OTPM). For example, an OTPM limit caps how many completion tokens your organization can generate per minute, regardless of how many input tokens are sent.\\n\\nIf these limits are configured on your account, you'll see your TPM value on the Limits page — hover over it to see the \\\"X in / Y out\\\" breakdown. If no breakdown appears, your organization has a single combined TPM cap with no separate input/output limits.\\n\\n## Rate Limits\\n\\nThe following is a high level summary and there may be exceptions to these limits. You can view the current, exact rate limits for your organization on the limits page in your account settings.\\n\\nNeed higher rate limits? Upgrade to Developer plan to access higher limits, Batch and Flex processing, and more.                 continue
        before = text[max(0, match.start() - 4) : match.start()]''')

def test_date_shaped_transfer_reference_is_removed():

    assert len(result.records) == 1
    assert result.records[0].amount == -100
    assert result.records[0].balance == 900
'''

const notes = "# NOTES — PJ Bank API\n\nI <NATIONAL_ID> a local span-based scrubber because the task requires removing identifiers while keeping names, merchants, dates, and amounts. Rules combine labeled context, IBAN mod-97, Luhn, phonenumbers, and date/amount exclusions. Overlap resolution keeps replacements stable and idempotent. I considered Presidio, scrubadub, spaCy NER, and LLM redaction; name redaction and extra model dependencies made them poor defaults for this brief. pdfplumber, python-docx, and charset-normalizer cover the supplied formats.\n\n## API and storage\n\n`POST /api/v1/batches` extracts, scrubs, parses, and commits a batch together. Subresources expose scrubbed text, transactions, versioned analyses, and chat sessions. The CLI accepts local folders; HTTP endpoints accept uploads so clients cannot choose server filesystem paths. Duplicate filenames receive distinct names before parsing, keeping file links and citations separate.\n\nPostgreSQL separates batches, files, redaction counts, transactions, analyses, sessions, and messages. It stores scrubbed text and derived data; no raw statement column exists. UUIDs identify resources, `NUMERIC(18,2)` stores amounts, JSONB holds facts/reports, and foreign keys cascade deletions. Transactions support filtering and deterministic aggregation without asking the model to calculate totals.\n\n## Groq and prompts\n\nI <NATIONAL_ID> `openai/gpt-oss-120b` for reasoning and JSON output, with `openai/gpt-oss-20b` as a faster fallback. Groq lists a 131,072-token context and roughly 500 tokens/sec for 120b. Its published 8K TPM quota constrains this demo before the context window does. Free-tier access avoids inference charges within the account allowance; paid 120b pricing is $0.15 input/$0.60 output per million tokens. [Models](https://console.groq.com/docs/models), [limits](https://console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits), checked 29 October 2026.\n\nThe exact system prompts and JSON schemas are in [app/services/llm/prompts.py](app/services/llm/prompts.py). The central instruction is “FACTS are the ONLY source of truth for numbers.” The prompts forbid invented transactions, require separate currencies and source refs, treat statement/context blocks as untrusted data, and tell chat to refuse unsupported questions. Analysis receives compact facts, a scrubbed excerpt, and a transaction digest. Chat receives facts, retrieved rows, the analysis narrative, and recent history.\n\n## Accuracy, verification, and limits\n\nPython computes totals and rankings. Validation checks numeric values against facts/transactions and re-grounds analysis citations by category, merchant, and currency. Unsupported output gets one repair retry, then a deterministic answer or refusal. Numeric membership cannot prove every sentence’s meaning or every date claim.\n\nComplete prompts, including history and repairs, pass the residual scanner before transport. All model strings are scrubbed before validation/storage, including refusal and error metadata. Upload limits apply after ZIP expansion. Tests cover leaks, preservation, timestamp-shaped references, negative balances, mixed currencies, source collisions, malformed output, and API persistence: 55 pass. Browser checks cover the frontend and live Groq separately.\n\nScanned PDFs need OCR; addresses depend on labels; unusual IDs/layouts need more rules. Next I would add country-specific fixtures, OCR, migrations, and background analysis jobs.\n";

const reviewExporter = String.raw`from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from scripts.export_ai_transcript import SECRET_RE, redact  # noqa: E402

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def _block(text: str) -> str:
    longest = max((len(match.group()) for match in re.finditer(r" +\"`\"+String.raw`+", text)), default=0)
    fence = " +\"`\"+String.raw`" * max(3, longest + 1)
    return f"{fence}text\n{text}\n{fence}"


def export(session_path: Path) -> None:
    events = [json.loads(line) for line in session_path.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]
    models = sorted({event["payload"]["model"] for event in events if event.get("type") == "turn_context" and event.get("payload", {}).get("model")})
    lines = [
        "# Codex review transcript", "",
        "- Tool: OpenAI Codex",
        "- Model metadata: " + (", ".join(models) or "not recorded"),
        "- Subagents: none", "",
        "Export of saved user/assistant messages and tool calls/results through this snapshot. "
        "Private reasoning, platform instructions, and binary image data are excluded. "
        "PII and credentials are redacted locally; tool text is not shortened by this exporter. "
        "Run this exporter again after the final reply to include the completed conversation.", "",
    ]
    prompts = []
    for event in events:
        if event.get("type") != "response_item":
            continue
        item = event.get("payload") or {}
        kind = item.get("type")
        if kind == "message":
            role = item.get("role")
            if role not in {"user", "assistant"} or item.get("channel") == "analysis":
                continue
            text = "\n".join(str(part.get("text", "")) for part in item.get("content", []) if part.get("type") in {"input_text", "output_text", "text"})
            if not text.strip():
                continue
            safe = redact(text)
            lines.extend(["## " + role.capitalize(), "", safe, ""])
            if role == "user":
                prompts.append(safe)
        elif kind in {"function_call", "custom_tool_call"}:
            name = item.get("name", "tool")
            text = str(item.get("arguments", item.get("input", "")))
            lines.extend(["### Tool call: " + str(name), "", _block(redact(text)), ""])
        elif kind in {"function_call_output", "custom_tool_call_output"}:
            output = item.get("output", "")
            text = output if isinstance(output, str) else json.dumps(output, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
            lines.extend(["### Tool result", "", _block(redact(text)), ""])
    transcript = "\n".join(lines).strip() + "\n"
    if SECRET_RE.search(transcript):
        raise RuntimeError("Credential guard rejected transcript export.")
    (ROOT / "docs/AI_REVIEW_TRANSCRIPT.md").write_text(transcript)
    review_prompts = "\n\n---\n\n".join(prompts).strip() + "\n"
    (ROOT / "docs/AI_REVIEW_PROMPTS.txt").write_text(review_prompts)
    original_path = ROOT / "docs/AI_ORIGINAL_PROMPTS.txt"
    original = original_path.read_text() if original_path.exists() else (ROOT / "prompts.txt").read_text()
    (ROOT / "prompts.txt").write_text(original.strip() + "\n\n---\n\n" + review_prompts)
    print(f"Review export: {len(prompts)} user messages; {len(transcript)} characters; models={models}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Export a redacted Codex review without private reasoning.")
    parser.add_argument("session_jsonl", type=Path)
    export(parser.parse_args().session_jsonl)
`;

const script = String.raw`from pathlib import Path
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import Counter

root=Path("/home/muhammad-roshaan/dev/PROJ/pj-bank-api")
sys.path.insert(0,str(root))
from app.db import SessionLocal
from app.models import Batch, ChatMessage, ChatSession, Redaction, Transaction
from app.services.pipeline import process_folder
from app.services.scrubber.residual import scan_residual
from app.services.llm.client import sanitize_model_data
from app.services.llm.context import allowed_numbers, compact_facts, deterministic_analysis, markdown_from_result, validate_payload

result=process_folder(root/"data")
assert len(result.files)==4 and len(result.records)==119
assert not scan_residual(result.combined_text)
assert all(not scan_residual(file.scrub.text) for file in result.files if file.scrub)
expected={file.extracted.filename:file for file in result.files}
redactions=Counter()
for file in result.files:
    redactions.update(file.scrub.redaction_counts if file.scrub else {})
batch_meta=None
with SessionLocal() as db:
    batches=db.query(Batch).all()
    print("Demo database batches before correction:",len(batches))
    for batch in batches:
        files=list(batch.files)
        if len(files)!=len(expected) or {file.filename for file in files}!=set(expected):
            continue
        if any(file.sha256!=expected[file.filename].extracted.sha256 for file in files):
            continue
        transactions=list(batch.transactions)
        if len(transactions)!=len(result.records):
            raise RuntimeError("Sample batch transaction count differs; no migration applied.")
        by_source={(record.filename,record.line_no):record for record in result.records}
        for transaction in transactions:
            source=(transaction.file.filename,transaction.source_line)
            record=by_source[source]
            for attr in ("txn_date","txn_time","description","merchant","category","amount","currency","direction","balance"):
                setattr(transaction,attr,getattr(record,attr))
            transaction.meta={**record.meta,"ref":record.ref}
        for file in files:
            new=expected[file.filename]
            file.scrubbed_text=new.scrub.text
            file.redaction_counts=new.scrub.redaction_counts
            file.warnings=new.warnings
        batch.combined_text=result.combined_text
        batch.facts=result.facts
        batch.name=sanitize_model_data(batch.name)
        batch.raw_chars=sum(len(file.extracted.text) for file in result.files)
        batch.scrubbed_chars=sum(len(file.scrub.text) for file in result.files if file.scrub)
        batch.redaction_counts=dict(redactions)
        batch.warnings=result.warnings
        db.query(Redaction).filter(Redaction.batch_id==batch.id).delete(synchronize_session=False)
        for file in files:
            for finding in expected[file.filename].scrub.findings:
                db.add(Redaction(batch_id=batch.id,file_id=file.id,**finding))
        valid_refs=set(record.ref for record in result.records)
        allowed=allowed_numbers(result.facts,transactions)
        for analysis in batch.analyses:
            payload=sanitize_model_data(analysis.result)
            report=validate_payload(payload,valid_refs,allowed)
            if not report["grounded"]:
                payload=deterministic_analysis(result.facts)
                analysis.status="fallback"
                analysis.model="deterministic"
                payload["source"]="deterministic"
            payload["facts"]=compact_facts(result.facts)
            payload["validation"]=report if report["grounded"] else {"grounded":True,"source":"deterministic_fallback"}
            payload["model"]=analysis.model
            analysis.result=payload
            analysis.grounding_report=payload["validation"]
            analysis.markdown=markdown_from_result(payload)
            analysis.error=None
            assert not scan_residual(json.dumps(payload,ensure_ascii=False))
        for session in batch.chat_sessions:
            session.title=sanitize_model_data(session.title)
            for message in session.messages:
                message.content=sanitize_model_data(message.content)
                message.citations=sanitize_model_data(message.citations)
                message.grounding=sanitize_model_data(message.grounding)
        batch_meta={"id":str(batch.id),"name":batch.name}
        print("Corrected sample batch; files:",len(files),"transactions:",len(transactions),"analyses:",len(batch.analyses),"sessions:",len(batch.chat_sessions))
    db.commit()

# Regenerate public outputs from the corrected pipeline without creating demo batches.
completed=subprocess.run([str(root/".venv/bin/python"),"-m","app.cli","scrub","data","--out","outputs"],cwd=root,text=True,capture_output=True,check=True)
print(completed.stdout.strip())
if batch_meta:
    p=root/"outputs/metadata.json"
    meta=json.loads(p.read_text())
    meta.update(batch_id=batch_meta["id"],stored_in_postgres=True)
    p.write_text(json.dumps(meta,indent=2)+"\n")
    p=root/"outputs/redaction_report.json"
    report=json.loads(p.read_text())
    report.update(batch_id=batch_meta["id"],batch_name=batch_meta["name"])
    p.write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2,ensure_ascii=False)+"\n")
for p in [root/"outputs/scrubbed_combined.txt",*(root/"outputs/per_file").glob("*.scrubbed.txt")]:
    assert not scan_residual(p.read_text()),p.name
print("Combined/per-file outputs: residual scans clean.")
for name in ("README.md","NOTES.md","AGENTS.md","docs/GUARDRAILS.md"):
    p=root/name
    t=p.read_text().replace("55 tests","58 tests").replace("55 pass","58 pass").replace("55 automated tests","58 automated tests").replace("currently 55","currently 58").replace("tests (55)","tests (58)")
    t=t.replace("3K-character","2K-character").replace("3K-char","2K-char")
    t=t.replace("complete transaction digest","bounded transaction digest (complete for the provided sample)")
    t=t.replace("full transaction\n  digest","bounded transaction\n  digest")
    t=t.replace("(~6.2K input tokens; 1.2K output)","(measure input plus the 1.2K output allowance before adding context)")
    p.write_text(t)
print("Updated documentation for 58 tests and revised context bounds.")
`;

I considered Presidio, scrubadub, spaCy NER, and LLM redaction; name redaction and extra model dependencies made them poor defaults for this brief. pdfplumber, python-docx, and charset-normalizer cover the supplied formats.\\n\\n## API and storage\\n\\n`POST /api/v1/batches` extracts, scrubs, parses, and commits a batch together. Subresources expose scrubbed text, transactions, versioned analyses, and chat sessions. The CLI accepts local folders; HTTP endpoints accept uploads so clients cannot choose server filesystem paths. Duplicate filenames receive distinct names before parsing, keeping file links and citations separate.\\n\\nPostgreSQL separates batches, files, redaction counts, transactions, analyses, sessions, and messages. It stores scrubbed text and derived data; no raw statement column exists. UUIDs identify resources, `NUMERIC(18,2)` stores amounts, JSONB holds facts/reports, and foreign keys cascade deletions. Free-tier access avoids inference charges within the account allowance; paid 120b pricing is $0.15 input/$0.60 output per million tokens. [Models](https://console.groq.com/docs/models), [limits](https://console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits), checked 29 October 2026.\\n\\nThe exact system prompts and JSON schemas are in [app/services/llm/prompts.py](app/services/llm/prompts.py). The central instruction is “FACTS are the ONLY source of truth for numbers.” The prompts forbid invented transactions, require separate currencies and source refs, treat statement/context blocks as untrusted data, and tell chat to refuse unsupported questions. Analysis receives compact facts, a scrubbed excerpt, and a transaction digest. Chat receives facts, retrieved rows, the analysis narrative, and recent history.\\n\\n## Accuracy, verification, and limits\\n\\nPython computes totals and rankings. Validation checks numeric values against facts/transactions and re-grounds analysis citations by category, merchant, and currency. Unsupported output gets one repair retry, then a deterministic answer or refusal. Numeric membership cannot prove every sentence’s meaning or every date claim.\\n\\nComplete prompts, including history and repairs, pass the residual scanner before transport. All model strings are scrubbed before validation/storage, including refusal and error metadata. Upload limits apply after ZIP expansion. Tests cover leaks, preservation, timestamp-shaped references, negative balances, mixed currencies, source collisions, malformed output, and API persistence: 58 pass. Browser checks cover the frontend and live Groq separately.\\n\\nScanned PDFs need OCR; addresses depend on labels; unusual IDs/layouts need more rules. const script = String.raw`from pathlib import Path
import json
import os
import re
import runpy
import subprocess
import sys
import zipfile

root=Path("/home/muhammad-roshaan/dev/PROJ/pj-bank-api")
sys.path.insert(0,str(root))
from app.config import settings
from app.db import SessionLocal
from app.models import Analysis, Batch, ChatSession, Transaction
from app.services.scrubber.residual import scan_residual

pii=runpy.run_path(str(root/"tests/test_scrubber.py"))["KNOWN_PII"]
for p in [root/"outputs/scrubbed_combined.txt",*(root/"outputs/per_file").glob("*.scrubbed.txt")]:
    content=p.read_text()
    assert not scan_residual(content),p.name
    assert all(value not in content for value in pii),p.name

secret=re.compile(r"\b(?:gsk_|gho_|github_pat_)[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b")
for name in ("docs/AI_TRANSCRIPT.md","docs/AI_TRANSCRIPT_FULL.md","docs/AI_REVIEW_TRANSCRIPT.md","docs/AI_ORIGINAL_PROMPTS.txt","docs/AI_REVIEW_PROMPTS.txt","prompts.txt"):
    p=root/name
    text=p.read_text()
    matches=[value for value in pii if value in text]
    assert not matches,(name,"Known PII remains; values withheld.")
    assert not secret.search(text),(name,"Credential pattern remains.")
print("Public transcripts/prompts: known-PII and credential checks passed.")

unsafe_env={**os.environ,"TEST_DATABASE_URL":"postgresql+psycopg://pjbank:<EMAIL>:5432/pjbank"}
unsafe=subprocess.run([str(root/".venv/bin/python"),"-m","pytest","--collect-only","-q"],cwd=root,env=unsafe_env,text=True,capture_output=True)
assert unsafe.returncode!=0 and "isolated PostgreSQL" in unsafe.stderr+unsafe.stdout
print("Unsafe test-database target refused before fixture execution.")

qa_env={**os.environ,"DATABASE_URL":settings.test_database_url}
cli=subprocess.run([str(root/".venv/bin/python"),"-m","app.cli","scrub","data","--out","/tmp/pj-bank-cli-review","--store"],cwd=root,env=qa_env,text=True,capture_output=True,check=True)
meta=json.loads(Path("/tmp/pj-bank-cli-review/metadata.json").read_text())
assert meta["file_count"]==4 and meta["transaction_count"]==119 and meta["stored_in_postgres"]
print("CLI --store: four files and 119 transactions persisted to isolated PostgreSQL.")
with SessionLocal() as db:
    batches=db.query(Batch).all()
    assert len(batches)==1
    batch=batches[0]
    assert batch.file_count==4
    assert db.query(Transaction).filter(Transaction.batch_id==batch.id).count()==119
    assert db.query(Analysis).filter(Analysis.batch_id==batch.id).count()==1
    assert db.query(ChatSession).filter(ChatSession.batch_id==batch.id).count()==0
    assert not scan_residual(batch.combined_text)
print("Demo database: one batch, four files, 119 transactions, one analysis, no chat sessions.")

skip_dirs={".git",".venv","data","__pycache__",".pytest_cache",".ruff_cache","node_modules"}
files=[]
for folder,dirs,names in os.walk(root):
    dirs[:]=[name for name in dirs if name not in skip_dirs]
    for name in names:
        path=Path(folder)/name
        if name==".env" or (name.startswith(".env.") and name!=".env.example"):
            continue
        if path.suffix.lower() in {".pyc",".pyo",".log",".db",".sqlite",".sqlite3",".mp4",".mov"}:
            continue
        content=path.read_bytes()
        assert not (settings.groq_api_key and settings.groq_api_key.encode() in content),(str(path.relative_to(root)),"Configured key found.")
        assert not secret.search(content.decode("utf-8",errors="ignore")),(str(path.relative_to(root)),"Credential pattern found.")
        files.append(path)
zip_path=root.parent/"pj-bank-api-submission.zip"
temporary=zip_path.with_suffix(".zip.tmp")
with zipfile.ZipFile(temporary,"w",zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED,compresslevel=9) as archive:
    for path in sorted(files):
        archive.write(path,Path(root.name)/path.relative_to(root))
with zipfile.ZipFile(temporary) as archive:
    assert archive.testzip() is None
    for path in files:
        arcname=str(Path(root.name)/path.relative_to(root))
        assert archive.read(arcname)==path.read_bytes(),arcname
    assert all(not (set(Path(name).parts)&skip_dirs) for name in archive.namelist())
temporary.replace(zip_path)
print("ZIP verified:",len(files),"files;",zip_path.stat().st_size,"bytes; private data/runtime/video excluded.")
`;

const js = String.raw`const assert=require("node:assert/strict");
const {chromium}=require("/tmp/opencode/pw/node_modules/playwright-core");
(async()=>{
  const browser=await chromium.launch({executablePath:"/usr/bin/google-chrome",headless:true,args:["--no-sandbox","--disable-dev-shm-usage","--disable-renderer-backgrounding","--disable-background-timer-throttling"]});
  const page=await browser.newPage({viewport:{width:1440,height:1000}});
  const errors=[];
  page.on("pageerror",error=>errors.push(error.message));
  await page.goto("http://<IP_ADDRESS>:8001/",{waitUntil:"networkidle"});
  const batches=await (await page.request.get("http://<IP_ADDRESS>:8001/api/v1/batches")).json();
  let selected;
  for(const batch of batches){
    const response=await page.request.get("http://<IP_ADDRESS>:8001/api/v1/batches/"+batch.id+"/analysis");
    if(response.status()===200){selected={batch:await(await page.request.get("http://<IP_ADDRESS>:8001/api/v1/batches/"+batch.id)).json(),analysis:await response.json()};break;}
  }
  assert.ok(selected,"A live analysis is required for responsive verification");
  await page.evaluate(({batch,analysis})=>{
    state.batch=batch;
    state.fileDetails=batch.files.map(file=>({...file,scrubbed_text:"Verified scrubbed output."}));
    renderBatch();
    renderAnalysis(analysis);
    appendMessage("assistant","Verified budget facts.",{grounded:true,citations:["international_bank_statements_apr2026.docx:103"]});
  },selected);
  for(const width of [320,390,760,1440]){
    await page.setViewportSize({width,height:1000});
    const sizes=await page.evaluate(()=>({viewport:innerWidth,document:document.documentElement.scrollWidth}));
    assert.ok(sizes.document<=sizes.viewport+1,JSON.stringify(sizes));
    console.log("Responsive viewport "+width+": no horizontal page overflow");
  }
  await page.setViewportSize({width:390,height:844});
  await page.evaluate(()=>scrollTo({top:0,behavior:"instant"}));
  await page.screenshot({path:"/tmp/pj-bank-review-mobile.png"});
  await page.evaluate(()=>document.querySelector("#analysis-output").scrollIntoView({behavior:"instant",block:"start"}));
  await page.screenshot({path:"/tmp/pj-bank-review-mobile-analysis.png"});
  assert.deepEqual(errors,[]);
  await browser.close();
  console.log("Responsive checks passed; no page errors");
})().catch(error=>{console.error(error);process.exit(1);});
`;

import json
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,"/home/muhammad-roshaan/dev/PROJ/pj-bank-api")
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from app.config import settings
from app.models import Analysis, Batch
from app.services.llm.client import GroqLLM
import app.services.llm.chat as service
usage=[]
class MetricsLLM(GroqLLM):
    def _call(self,*args,**kwargs):
        result=super()._call(*args,**kwargs)
        usage.append({"model":result.model,"usage":result.usage})
        print("Live chat input tokens:",result.usage.get("prompt_tokens"),"model:",result.model,flush=True)
        return result
service.GroqLLM=MetricsLLM
engine=create_engine(settings.test_database_url)
with Session(engine) as db:
    analysis=db.query(Analysis).filter(Analysis.status=="completed").order_by(Analysis.created_at.desc()).first()
    assert analysis is not None
    batch=db.get(Batch,analysis.batch_id)
    _,message,payload=service.chat(db,batch,"How much did I spend on food?")
    report={"model":message.model,"source":message.grounding.get("source"),"grounded":payload["grounded"],"calls":usage}
    Path("/tmp/pj_bank_chat_usage.json").write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2))
    print("Food chat:",report["model"],"source:",report["source"],"grounded:",report["grounded"],flush=True)
    assert report["source"]=="groq"
    assert report["grounded"]
`;
